subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should per-job and heartbeat elevated exec be solved as a narrow elevated marker, or folded into the broader Gateway-owned scheduling provenance model?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes host-exec authority, cron persistence, heartbeat provenance, config compatibility, and migration behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent trust model.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat this as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement narrow elevated markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat elevated authority fields now, with explicit create/update/execution audit semantics and migration proof.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove cron-event and heartbeat wildcard elevation only if maintainers accept the compatibility break and provide recovery guidance.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat this as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest recent feature-history signal is joshavant's merged cron caller-scope work in PR 96883.
